key_insight: ScaleToT shows that structured reasoning learned from a small set of LLM-processed users can be generalized to billion-scale low-activity users without running LLM inference on everyone.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path to deploy high-quality user modeling at advertising scale by combining sparse-profile reasoning, lightweight encoders, and reduced compute cost.
method: Builds typed user-state chains with bounded-entropy Tree-of-Thought refinement to improve reasoning reliability.
Uses teacher-curated chains to train a student model from static profiles via supervised fine-tuning and OSIPO.
Transfers the student’s reasoning signals to a lightweight profile encoder for population-wide deployment without LLM inference.
evidence_signal: In a billion-scale advertising deployment, the randomized online A/B test increased LT30 by 6.738%, while offline reasoning covered only 7.32% of the potential population.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and representativeness of the small LLM-processed subset, so sparse or biased teacher data could limit generalization.
paper_title: ScaleToT: Generalizing Structured LLM Reasoning for Billion-Scale Low-Activity User Modeling
